policy.last_change: 4 Mar 2026 (-25bp, eff. 5 Mar); held 9 Apr, 6 May and 2 Jun

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 12 Jun close (1x4 3.86, 3x6 3.90, 6x9 4.02, 9x12 4.16 vs WIBOR 3M 3.86) price roughly 30bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. Dąbrowski (12 Jun, Bloomberg): a cut is now more likely than a hike, most members are more optimistic on inflation. May flash CPI 3.1% (29 May; 3.7% expected, -0.3% m/m on food); core 3.0% in April. The fuel VAT cut and price caps run to 30 June, but the excise cut ends on 15 June; Tusk: the fuel package ends in summer.
policy.risk_text: MPC members now call cuts more likely than hikes (Masłowska 9 Jun, Dąbrowski 10 Jun) while the ECB hiked on 11 Jun and the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike; risks: the Iran deal failing, the fuel package ending (excise 15 Jun, VAT after 30 Jun) and two PLN 6-12bn sales (17, 24 Jun).

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027; Fitch (8 Jun): GDP 3.3%, NBP flat at 3.75% to year-end; World Bank (11 Jun): GDP 3.1% / 2.6%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after April PLN 89.3bn (30.1% of the limit); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; EDP debt 61.6% of GDP at end-Q1 (10 Jun); 2027 budget path (9 Jun): GDP 3.1%, CPI 2.5%; windfall-tax draft cut to a 60% rate, PLN 3.8bn in 2026 (11 Jun); fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps) to 30 June, excise cut ends 15 June.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~56% (MoF, 29 May) financed; budget accounts PLN 208.3bn at end-May (MoF, 8 Jun); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P A-/stable (affirmed 8 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks; Fitch's June forecast round (8 Jun) was not a rating action.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 12-14 Jun: April C/A deficit EUR 1.56bn vs ~0.34bn expected (fuel imports; 12M 0.9% of GDP, ING). Dabrowski (Bloomberg): a cut is now more likely than a hike; most MPC members more optimistic on inflation. The fuel VAT cut runs to 30 Jun but the excise cut ends (from 15 Jun); Tusk: CPN to end in summer. BGK: Q3 issuance to prefund 2027 FPC needs (~30% secured). PKO: an Iran deal could take the 10Y to ~5.55%. Abroad: MoU terms emerged (immediate Hormuz reopening, phased sanctions relief, a 60-day truce incl. Lebanon) amid Iranian denials; late Sunday Trump said a deal was reached, Hormuz open and the blockade lifted, signing 19 June. Brent ~$87 (-6% w/w), Bund 10Y <3%, gilt <4.8%; UK April GDP -0.1%; UMich 48.9; Romania May CPI 10.9%, Vestea named PM; a September ECB hike priced.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 17 Jun, 24 Jun. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: the ECB has started hiking (11 Jun) while a US-Iran deal takes shape; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 30bp of NBP hikes; the ECB hiked to 2.25% on 11 Jun with one more hike priced, the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike, the BoE is priced for hikes, the CNB is on hold and the MNB is on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 52bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 261bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 12 Jun close). Trump: Iran deal, Hormuz open (12-14 Jun).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK: Q3 issuance will mainly prefund the FPC's 2027 needs (~30% secured, 12 Jun); EUR 2bn priced on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
